description: The figure is a two-level (nested) pie/donut chart representing a breakdown of character types used in the referenced paper, first by broad category and then by subtypes within those categories. The inner ring shows three slices: “Virtual Characters” in blue occupying the majority (roughly about two-thirds), “Real Characters” in light green taking a smaller portion (around one-fifth), and “Custom Characters” in pink making up the remaining share (around one-sixth). The outer ring subdivides these: the blue “Virtual Characters” portion is split into four labeled slices—“Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” and “Game Characters”—each shown in pale blue with no explicit percentages, with “Game Characters” appearing largest among them and the others smaller and similar in size; the green “Real Characters” portion is split into seven pale-green slices labeled “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” “Actors,” and “Influencers,” each a thin segment with no printed percentages; and the pink “Custom Characters” portion appears as a single outer pink segment corresponding to the inner “Custom Characters” slice. There is no visible legend and no percentage labels inside slices, and no segments appear exploded or otherwise emphasized beyond color and labeling; the outer segments appear arranged around the circle rather than clearly ordered by size.
